# Pipeline bits

Uprating listed rents - attempt to do this with fixed effects.
Problem: there will be boroughs (City of London likely) with few repeated observations, where the borough-year effects will not be calculated.
Could do instead: something like a spatial regression with an adaptive bandwidth instead of a borough fixed effect?
Advantage of this approach: consistent in a sense that I am estimating what the listing price in a given year would be

```{python}
listings = pd.read_parquet(HASP_DIRECTORY / "wfz_rent_listings.parquet")
properties = pd.read_parquet(HASP_DIRECTORY / "wfz_rent_properties.parquet")

listings["property_id"].nunique()
listings.groupby(["property_id"]).size().value_counts()
listings["source_year"].value_counts().sort_index()
listings.groupby(["property_id","source_year"]).size().value_counts()

presence = pd.crosstab(listings["property_id"], listings["source_year"])
overlap = presence.T.dot(presence)

# Download and assemble a postcode lookup
postcodes = pd.read_parquet("/Users/benito/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-LondonSchoolofEconomics/PhD/rent-project/data/raw/lookups/onspd_aug_2026.parquet")

# merge lad code into rent_properties into rent_listings
listings_lad = (
    listings
    .merge(properties[["property_id","postcode"]], how="left", on="property_id")
    .merge(postcodes[["pcds","lad26cd"]], how="left", left_on="postcode", right_on="pcds")
)

# checking it worked
listings_lad["lad26cd"].value_counts(dropna=False) # 33
listings_lad["lad26cd"].value_counts(dropna=False).sum() # 1549791
listings_lad["lad26cd"].isna().sum() #0

# data prep
df = listings_lad[["property_id", "lad26cd", "source_year", "listed_price"]]
df["log_price"] = np.log(df["listed_price"])
df["la_year"] = df["lad26cd"] + "_" + df["source_year"].astype(str)

years = sorted(df["source_year"].unique())

# fit fixed effects on rent_listings
model = pf.feols("log_price ~ 1 | property_id + la_year", data=df)
gamma = pd.Series(model.fixef()["C(la_year)"])      # borough-year effects

df["alpha_part"] = df["log_price"] - df["la_year"].map(gamma)
props = df.groupby("property_id").agg(alpha=("alpha_part", "mean"), lad26cd=("lad26cd", "first")).reset_index()

# estimate 2011, 2021, 2024 rent for each property

for year in years:
    props[f"estimated_rent_{year}"] = np.exp(props["alpha"] + (props["lad26cd"] + f"_{year}").map(gamma))


# then merge into spine either: actually existing or estimated rent for the three years

```

```{python}

    spine[spine["is_residential_2021"]]

)

    spine[spine["is_residential_2026"]]
    .groupby("lad21cd")

    .rename_axis("lad_cd").reset_index()

    .assign(year=2026)
)

dwellings = pd.concat(
    [dwellings_2011, dwellings_2021, dwellings_2026],
    ignore_index=True
)
dwellings_long = dwellings.melt(
    id_vars=["lad_cd", "year"],
    value_vars=["spine", "ctsop"],
    var_name="source",
    value_name="dwellings",
)
dwellings_long["borough"] = dwellings_long["lad_cd"].map(LONDON_BOROUGHS)
```

Test HASP to AddressBase Links

THE MATCHING CODE ITSELF

```{python}
ADDRESS_COLUMNS = ['address_1', 'address_2', 'address_3', 'address_4', 'address_5', 'address_6']

spine = pd.read_parquet(ADDRESSBASE_DIRECTORY_INTERIM / "greater_london_abplus_spine.parquet")

addresses = pd.read_parquet(ADDRESSBASE_DIRECTORY_INTERIM / "greater_london_abplus_addresses.parquet")

rent_properties = pd.read_parquet(DATA_DIRECTORY / "raw" / "hasp-whenfresh-zoopla" / "wfz_rent_properties.parquet")


# preparing address to match
out = None
for col in ADDRESS_COLUMNS:
    s = rent_properties[col].astype('string')
    if out is None:
        out = s
    else:
        out = out.str.cat(s, sep=', ').fillna(out).fillna(s)
rent_properties['address'] = out.fillna('')
del out, s

# matcher
con = duckdb.connect()

hasp_addresses = con.from_df(
    rent_properties[["property_id","address","postcode"]]
    .rename(columns={"property_id": "unique_id", "address": "address_concat"})
)

addressbase_addresses = con.from_df(
    addresses[["uprn","address","postcode"]]
    .rename(columns={"uprn": "unique_id", "address": "address_concat"})
)

matcher = AddressMatcher(
    canonical_addresses=addressbase_addresses,
    addresses_to_match=hasp_addresses,
    con=con,
    stages=[
        ExactMatchStage(),
        PeeledAddressStage(),
        UniqueTrigramStage(),
        # SplinkStage(
        #    # recommended 10.0
        #    final_match_weight_threshold=10, 
        #    # recommended 1.0; initial testing: >2.0
        #    final_distinguishability_threshold=2.1, 
        #),
    ],
)
result = matcher.match()
rent_properties_matched = (
    result.matches().to_df()
    .rename(columns={
        "resolved_canonical_id": "uprn",
        "unique_id": "hasp_property_id"
    })
)

# PRECAUTIONS
# drop all unmatched
rent_properties_matched = rent_properties_matched.dropna(subset=["uprn"])
# drop repeated uprns (all instances)
rent_properties_matched = rent_properties_matched[
    ~rent_properties_matched.duplicated("uprn", keep=False)
]
# 655136 - 2489 - 2501 = 650146


# LAST STEP

# Merging the hasp property id to addresses spine
spine_hasp = spine.merge(
    rent_properties_matched[["hasp_property_id","uprn"]],
    how='left', on="uprn")
# make sure to add a check that spine has not gotten longer
# 4151457 to 4159941, due to uprn duplicates in hasp
# stays 4151457 after dropping uprn duplicates in hasp

# These checks should defo be included in some output, maybe by borough:
len(spine_hasp[~spine_hasp["hasp_property_id"].isna()])
# 650146 as expected
len(spine_hasp[~spine_hasp["hasp_property_id"].isna()]) / len(spine_hasp)
# 16% properties has hasp_property_id
```

```{python}
)
matched_probabilistic_sample.to_csv(ADDRESSBASE_DIRECTORY_INTERIM / "matched_hasp_to_ab_probabilistic_sample_inspection.csv")
```

What proportion of (allocated) PRS dwelling totals has listings (in 2021, by LSOA21, distribution)

```{python}
data = pd.read_parquet(PROCESSED_DIRECTORY / "greater_london_rents_dataset.parquet")

rented_2021 = data[
    (data["is_residential_2021"] == True)
    & (data["state_2021"].eq("2") | data["state_2021"].isna())
    & (data["private_rented_2021"] == True)
]
len(rented_2021) # 1,174,022
rented_2021["est_rent_imputed"].sum() # 553,926
1 - (rented_2021["est_rent_imputed"].sum() / len(rented_2021)) # 0.528 has a listing


# by LSOA
by_lsoa = (
    rented_2021
    .groupby("lsoa21cd")[["private_rented_2021", "est_rent_imputed"]]
    .sum()
)
by_lsoa = by_lsoa[by_lsoa["private_rented_2021"] > 0]
by_lsoa["prop_w_listing"] = 1 - (by_lsoa["est_rent_imputed"] / by_lsoa["private_rented_2021"])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
ax.hist(by_lsoa["prop_w_listing"], bins=50, edgecolor="white")
ax.set_xlabel("Proportion of private rented properties with a listing")
ax.set_ylabel("Number of LSOAs")
ax.set_title("Proportion of private rented properties with a listing")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

by_lsoa["prop_w_listing"].mean() # 0.567
by_lsoa["prop_w_listing"].median() # 0.565

```
